newsitem.title: USA: EU GMO segregation proposal has lost momentum-USDA.
newsitem.headline: EU GMO segregation proposal has lost momentum-USDA.

text.p: A proposal by European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to segregate genetically modified organisms has "lost a great deal of momentum" and EU commissioners will meet next week to discuss new proposals for labelling, a U.S. Agriculture Department official said Friday.

"Our understanding is that that proposal has lost a great deal of momentum because it went much farther than was realistic for anybody," said Paul Drazek, USDA trade adviser. "It would have caused major disruptions in the market."
Drazek spent Monday in Brussels meeting with EU officials ahead of their summer holiday.
"So they're looking for alternatives and we're watching closely," said Drazek. "We're still very very anxious about all the proposals that are floating around Brussels on labelling."
He said it was possible the EU might make a decision on labelling next week.
EU's Fischler had argued that genetically-altered farm products must be separated otherwise consumers could not be sure about the type of food they were purchasing.
